messages:
Maya (Support): FYI — just got a customer escalation. Multiple services in eu-west are getting sudden 429s and the app spikes errors around 12:04 UTC. They included a few snippets.
Maya (Support): customer says: 'we started getting 429s after your deploy at 12:02, then billing shows repeated small charges for the same request ids'
Maya (Support): request sample header they pasted: 
```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer sk-customer-xxx
Content-Type: application/json
x-region: eu-west-1
x-request-id: req_0a1b2c
```

Maya (Support): response they saw: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1649999999
x-request-id: req_0a1b2c
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "retry_after": 0
}
```

Maya (Support): they also attached a log line showing our side returning 429 but billing meters show 1 token consumed per retry, looks like double counting when retries happen.
ops-bot: incident created — id: LIM-2026-03-15-001, severity: P2, channel: #eng-sre. Runbook: https://confluence/internal/runbooks/limiter
Raj (SRE): on it. Which deploy went out at 12:02? Anyone know PR/commit?
Lina (Eng Runtime): Deploy tag runtime-service@v3.8.2 rolled at 11:58 with a canary. Promoted at ~12:01. I pushed a limiter config tweak in that change — trying to find the diff.
Lina (Eng Runtime): config snippet from the deploy: 
```
limiters:
  default:
    type: token_bucket
    capacity: 100
    refill_rate: 100/s
    burst: 0    # explicitly set to 0 in this deploy
    scope: token
    backend: redis
```

Raj (SRE): burst: 0? That stands out. Previously burst was 200 for this tenant profile. Setting burst=0 will make short bursts impossible and could cause strong 429s when traffic spikes. Did we intend to change that?
Lina (Eng Runtime): I changed burst=0 to tighten steady-state throughput for beta customers. Guess I missed per-tenant overrides. My bad.
Tom (Billing): The billing duplication might be because retries are being counted as separate billable units before the limiter rejects — especially if we accept and meter a request before limiter denies at another layer. Need to see where metering hooks run relative to limiter.
Raj (SRE): pulling redis keys for limiter now. Using tenant key: limiter:tenant:acct-123.
Raj (SRE): redis GET limiter:tenant:acct-123 -> current_tokens = -5 (wtf), last_refill=1700000000
Raj (SRE): negative tokens indicates race or double-decrement. We use a lua script to check-and-decrement but there was a fallback path in C that decremented separately when redis timed out. Need logs for redis timeouts.
Lina (Eng Runtime): I found the change — I refactored the fallback path to return a 429 quickly on redis errors, but I mistakenly left an asynchronous code path that decremented local in-memory counters before redis confirmation. If redis later failed, the metrics showed decremented tokens but redis didn't reflect it -> mismatch.
Maya (Support): customer is on bursty traffic pattern (webhooks) so burst=0 would surface immediately. They sent a replay of 60 requests in 5s.
ops-bot: metric alert: limiter-error-rate eu-west increased from 0.1% -> 3.5% at 12:03 UTC.
Raj (SRE): short mitigation plan: 1) revert config change (set burst back to 200) 2) disable the new async decrement fallback 3) patch meter ordering so billing happens after limiter decision 4) emergency redis lua fix (atomic check) 5) notify customer and offer credits
Lina (Eng Runtime): rolling a hotfix now: runtime-service@v3.8.3 — will set burst: 200 and disable async fallback. Deploying to canary in eu-west first.
Raj (SRE): while that deploy is in progress, we should enable the per-tenant circuit-fallback that sends to the low-cost queued path so we avoid immediate 429s for the customer. I can flip the routing flag for acct-123.
Tom (Billing): I've paused automatic billing for that tenant for requests between 12:02-12:10, will reconcile after we confirm correct metering. I'll also open a billing ticket to credit duplicate charges.
Lina (Eng Runtime): pushing the hotfix now. Canary logs: 
```
[12:05:10] limiter: tenant=acct-123 action=check result=ok tokens=150
[12:05:10] request=req_0a1b2c routed=normal
```

Raj (SRE): canary looks good. I'm promoting the hotfix to eu-west-prod.
ops-bot: deploy started runtime-service@v3.8.3 -> eu-west
Lina (Eng Runtime): patch note: replace non-atomic decrement with redis EVAL script: 
```
local k = KEYS[1]
local cost = tonumber(ARGV[1])
local cap = tonumber(redis.call('GET', k) or '0')
if cap >= cost then
  redis.call('DECRBY', k, cost)
  return 1
end
return 0
```

Raj (SRE): verify: after patch, redis keys show tokens >= 0. No negatives. Good.
Maya (Support): customer acknowledged receipt, ran quick smoke — reduced 429s, still sees a couple.
Lina (Eng Runtime): those couple were due to remaining per-edge caching TTLs where old config still in memory for a node. Flushing node cache should fix. Rolling restart of the 3 nodes with stale config.
Raj (SRE): restarted nodes, 429 rate dropped to baseline.
Tom (Billing): billing logs show duplicates stopped after 12:07. I've queued refunds for duplicates, will follow up with finance.
Maya (Support): Customer confirmed recovery and appreciated proactive credits. They asked for root cause summary and a mitigation plan.
Lina (Eng Runtime): root cause: misconfigured limiter change (burst=0) + a regression where an async fallback path performed local decrements before redis confirm -> race led to negative token states and uncoordinated metering leading to duplicate billing on retries.
Raj (SRE): mitigation actions (short-term): 
- revert burst to previous per-tenant defaults for all sensitive tenants (completed)
- disable async fallback path (completed)
- atomic redis lua for check-and-decrement (deployed)
- enable queued fallback for bursty tenants (enabled for acct-123)
- billing pause + credits (Tom owns)

Raj (SRE): long-term: 
- add integration test that simulates redis timeouts + race to catch async decrement paths
- add alert for negative token values and divergence between in-memory and redis counts
- move billing meter to fire after limiter decision (Tom/Lina)
- runbook update: add steps for quick revert of limiter params and tenant-level routing

ops-bot: post-incident task created: LIM-2026-03-15-001-RT. Postmortem owner: Raj. Due: 2026-03-22.
Maya (Support): assigning customer follow-up to me, I'll send the summary + credit note and link to postmortem when available.
Lina (Eng Runtime): opening a PR with the tests and runbook changes. Will tag for Raj review.
Tom (Billing): will confirm refunds processed by EOD and post update to this thread.
Raj (SRE): thanks all. Nice quick coordination. We should include the specific config diff in the postmortem and note "avoid burst=0 for bursty tenants" as a lesson.
Maya (Support): closing loop with customer in 30m.
Tom (Billing): refunds processed. Ticket closed.
Raj (SRE): postmortem drafted, link: https://confluence/internal/postmortems/LIM-2026-03-15-001 — please review comments by EOD.
Maya (Support): confirmed customer satisfied. marking as resolved in support tracker. :white_check_mark:
